DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

The Diary Beside the Declaration

STS-HS11-L3-10001300-HSELA1112-HJD-MNA-01 • HS English 11-12 • Foundational U.S. Documents: Themes, Purposes, and Rhetorical Features
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Historical journals let a reader stand inside a moment instead of reading about it. Layla, Tarek, and Rania are pairing invented diary entries from a family who arrived from Beirut and Casablanca with the exact lines those readers met for the first time in English. A diary says I felt. The Declaration says we hold.
Which one persuades a stranger more, and what does each one want from its reader?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Layla doing?
Look at the picture. Can you say what Layla is doing and why she is doing it, in two complete sentences that connect to each other?
2
What is Tarek holding?
Look at the picture. Can you say what Tarek has in his hands and why he is holding it up, in two complete sentences that connect to each other?
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Can you say what the teacher is doing and why she is doing it, in two complete sentences that connect to each other?
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Can you say what kind of room this is and how you can tell, in two complete sentences that connect to each other?
5
Tell me about the exhibit wall.
Look at the picture. Can you say what is on the big wall and why it is up there, in two complete sentences that connect to each other?
6
What is Rania wearing?
Look at the picture. Can you say what Rania has on and why she might be wearing it, in two complete sentences that connect to each other?
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
